calls.head: Sheltered vs. exposed
calls.body: On preventing dangerous shots, Los Angeles is one of the league’s best, but Montréal is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. The more dangerous chances should come at the Canadiens’ net.
calls.call: The Kings prevent dangerous shots better than the Canadiens do.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Doughty plays his 1,300th game as the Kings beat the Canadiens
paras: Alex Laferriere struck first for the Kings on the power play midway through the first. Los Angeles had a goal taken off for offside later in the period. Alex Newhook tied it up for Montréal early in the second, but that was the last goal the Canadiens would get. Los Angeles had another goal taken off for goalie interference midway through the period, but it didn’t cost them in the end. Trevor Moore put the Kings ahead for good later in the period. Dylan Larkin made his Canadiens debut, after twelve seasons with the Red Wings, and picked up an assist.

The Canadiens had a little more of the play, but the Kings had the finish. Darcy Kuemper made 29 saves for the Kings, and Jakub Dobeš stopped 20 of 22 at the other end. The Kings moved to 8-12-2, seventh in the Pacific, while the Habs dropped to 14-7-4, third in the Atlantic.

items.text: Artemi Panarin extended his point streak against Montréal to ten games.
The Kings’ Drew Doughty played his 1,300th NHL game.
Scott Laughton was in NHL.com’s projected lineup, but Alex Turcotte played instead.
Both of the preview’s calls held.
